key_insight: System-level defenses — not just model-side filters — are essential to prevent indirect prompt injection: agents need runtime architectures that enforce isolation, provenance, and dynamic security policies so untrusted data cannot covertly change agent goals or capabilities.
problem_solved: Addresses the vulnerability where malicious instructions embedded in untrusted data (indirect prompt injection) cause AI agents to take dangerous or undesired actions, by proposing system-level design principles to reduce attack surface and limit impact.
method: Design agent runtimes with isolation and capability restriction (sandboxing, fine-grained capability tokens) so untrusted inputs cannot directly alter core intent or privileged actions.
Enable dynamic replanning and runtime security-policy updates: agents monitor context and threat signals and adapt policies without relying solely on static prompts or offline filters.
Enforce provenance, strict parsing, and validation of external content to separate untrusted data from control instructions and to provide auditable traces for decisions.
impact: Provides practitioners pragmatic, architecture-level strategies to harden deployed agents against subtle instruction-based attacks, improving safety in real-world, dynamic environments where static prompt hygiene is insufficient.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing agent components: planner, executor, sandboxed modules, provenance/validator, and security-policy manager
Flowchart contrasting a vulnerable pipeline (untrusted data → model prompt → action) vs. defended pipeline (validation + sandbox + capability checks → action)
Icon set illustrating defenses: sandbox padlock, provenance badge, dynamic policy gear, and monitoring/alert bell

paper_title: Architecting Secure AI Agents: Perspectives on System-Level Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
paper_authors: Chong Xiang, Drew Zagieboylo, Shaona Ghosh, Sanjay Kariyappa, Kai Greshake
